sentences.text:
Ram Sevak Modi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10
February, 2021
Bench: A.M. Khanwilkar, Indu Malhotra, Ajay Rastogi

1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No(S).319/2011
 Ram Sevak Modi ...Appe
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh ...

Resp
 O R D E R

1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2.
Two broad points have been raised before us.
The first is about the genuineness and admissibility of document, being Annexure P-1 dated 16.08.1982.
The second is about the jurisdiction of the Food Inspector, Mr. N.S. Bhadoriya (PW-1) to inspect, search and carry out sampling of products/goods.
3. As regards the first point, there is nothing in the cross-examination of the prosecution witnesses to have challenged the stated document.
That was, therefore, admitted and allowed to be brought on record during the trial.

Notably, no such plea was taken before the trial Court, the Appellate Court,
and even the High Court.
The Counsel for the respondent-State justly submits that the document-annexure P-1 is a cover page, and not the report of the Food Inspector.
4. It is not necessary for us to examine the first ground any further as there is nothing in the evidence to suggest that the document was ever challenged by the appellant during the trial.

Hence,
this argument does not take the matter any further.
5. The second point urged before us is about the jurisdiction of Mr. N.S. Bhadoriya (PW-1), the Food Inspector, who carried out search/inspection and sampling.
This point has been exhaustively dealt with by the trial Court, and by the High Court.
The High Court has rightly noted that the Sessions Court proceeded on an erroneous basis by relying on a letter/circular, which was subsequent in point of time, after the sampling was already done.
Paragraph 15 of the impugned judgment deals with this aspect and rejected the argument of the appellant.
Accordingly, even this submission does not commend to us.

sentences.text: It is lastly submitted by the counsel for the appellant that the appellant has already reached the age of 70 years, and is not keeping good health.
That cannot be the basis to ignore the statutory minimum sentence provided under Section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, of not less than six months.
7. We find no reason to deviate from the conclusion reached by the High Court, hence this appeal fails, and is dismissed accordingly.

8. The appellant must surrender within four weeks, failing which, the local police officials are free to proceed against him in accordance with law.
9.
In view of the above all pending applications also stand disposed of.
(AJAY RASTOGI) NEW DELHI FEBRUARY 10, 2021.
